title: Choose a kernel bandwidth
description: You compare bandwidths with held-out density scores and plot the selected estimate.
source: draft: codex free model + edit: codex

steps.description: You keep the observations as the fitted model. To estimate density, you average Gaussian kernel values at distances scaled by bandwidth h, then divide by h.
You compute an initial bandwidth from the sample count and a spread estimate. The spread uses the smaller of standard deviation and the scaled interquartile range when that range is positive.

steps.question: Why does the bandwidth scoring code set the kernel matrix diagonal to zero?
steps.answer: Each diagonal entry compares a sample with itself. Setting it to zero makes each density score use the other n-1 samples.

steps.description: You score the supplied bandwidth candidates using mean log density. np.argmax selects the candidate with the highest score.
You evaluate the selected estimate on the supplied grid positions. The final chart overlays the density curve and a normalized histogram of the first standardized feature.
